title: Trace ghosting and focus-mode study - interaction notes
content:
Purpose:
Draft notes and interaction sketches for two related micro-interactions in the Trace Viewer: 'ghosting' (de-emphasizing non-relevant spans visually) and an explicit 'focus mode' that isolates a span lane and its direct subtree. Goal: reduce visual noise for engineers investigating request latencies while keeping context discoverable and keyboard-accessible.

Background / motivation:
- Observed user complaints in support threads and usability sessions: large traces are overwhelming; engineers often want to zero-in on one service or RPC and temporarily hide the rest without losing the ability to navigate back.
- Current filters (service / tag / duration) are too heavyweight for quick investigative flows; users repeatedly toggle multiple filters and lose spatial context.
- We want a lightweight, reversible mechanism that scales to 100s of spans in a trace while preserving trace timing relationships (waterfall axis) and allowing quick comparisons (focused span vs surrounding).

User problems we address:
1) Too many lanes/spans — hard to spot the critical path when spans with tiny durations or unrelated services fill the waterfall.
2) Losing temporal context — when users hide spans with current filters they often lose the visual relationships (start times / overlaps).
3) Keyboard-only workflows — power users navigate traces with keyboard; new interactions must be discoverable and unobtrusive.
4) Accessibility — contrast, screen-reader semantics, and focus order must be preserved.

Concepts / definitions used here:
- Ghosting: visually de-emphasize (fade to ~20-30% opacity + reduce hit target priority) spans and lanes that are not within the selected focus set. Ghosted spans remain present, measureable, and clickable, but recede visually.
- Focus mode: an explicit state that pins a lane/span and shows only that lane plus logical ancestors/descendants (configurable depth). Focus mode collapses unrelated lanes to the ghosted state and can optionally compact their vertical footprint.
- Direct subtree: for RPCs / batched operations we treat linked spans (by parent_id) as subtree; focus mode should allow toggling whether to include parallel siblings.

Interaction sketches (keyboard + mouse):
1) Quick hover + 'g' (ghost) keyboard shortcut:
   - Hovering on a span shows a faint toolbar with actions: inspect, pin, ghost, focus. Pressing 'g' toggles ghosting for the hovered span's service lane (all spans with same service).
   - Ghosting is additive: multiple ghosted services accumulate. 'Shift+g' toggles an inverse ghost (i.e., only these services remain full-contrast while others are ghosted).

2) Focus mode enter/exit:
   - Click the ellipsis on a span -> 'Focus' -> UI enters focus state: the selected span lane is full contrast, ancestors and direct children are medium contrast, all others ghosted and vertically compacted to 50% height. Timing axis remains absolute (no re-normalization) so overlaps remain legible.
   - Keyboard: select span with up/down, press 'f' to enter focus. Press 'Esc' to exit. Pressing 'Tab' cycles through focus toolbar actions.

3) Depth controls and 'spill' toggles:
   - Mini control in focus header: Depth: 0|1|2|All (defaults to 1). 'Spill siblings' toggle: when on, siblings that overlap the focused span visually expand to show context.

4) Ghost bar + mini legend:
   - Top-right of trace panel: small pill with count of ghosted spans (e.g., "5 ghosted"). Clicking opens a quick list to un-ghost specific services/spans or clear all. This reduces cognitive load of remembering what was ghosted.

Visual treatment rules:
- Full-contrast spans: baseline color + full stroke + elevation (shadow) on hover.
- Medium-contrast (ancestors/children): desaturated color, 60% opacity.
- Ghosted spans: 24% opacity, 1px stroke, pointer-events reduced so that click goes to nearest full-contrast span unless explicitly hovered.
- Compacting rule: Ghosted lanes compress to min height (18px) but still display timestamps; hovering or tabbing expands lane to full height.

Accessibility details:
- Screen-reader: entering focus mode should emit an aria-live message: "Focus mode entered on service X; depth 1; press Escape to exit."
- Keyboard focus: tab order moves to focus toolbar then to visible spans in reading order; ghosted spans are still reachable by keyboard (use Shift+Tab to reveal ghost).
- Color contrast: medium-contrast must meet AA contrast against background by adjusting saturation; do not rely on opacity alone. Provide alternative high-contrast toggle in accessibility settings.

Edge cases and tradeoffs:
- Performance: compacting and opacity changes must be GPU-accelerated CSS transforms for large traces. We should test on traces with 500+ spans. Potential fallback: disable animations when device reports 'prefers-reduced-motion'.
- Click targets: reducing pointer-events on ghosted spans improves click accuracy but can surprise users who expect to click them. Mitigation: show explicit tooltip on first ghost action explaining behavior and provide quick undo in toast.
- Correlated spans across lanes: services that are related (e.g., client/server pair) may be split across lanes; focus should optionally include 'correlated' spans by tracing tags (http.path, rpc.id). This requires heuristics and is an optional follow-up.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Toggle ghosting by service via 'g' on hover and top-right ghost pill shows count.
- Enter/exit focus by 'f' or via span menu; depth control supports 0/1/2.
- Visual states implemented for full/medium/ghosted with compacting.
- Keyboard bindings documented in keyboard shortcuts help modal.
- Performance target: interactive on traces with up to 300 spans on a standard laptop (macbook m1 equivalent) with <100ms frame drops on transitions.

Open questions / discussion points for design review:
1) Should ghosting be ephemeral (session-only) or persisted to trace-level annotations/shared links? Preferring ephemeral by default, with an option to 'Share view' that records ghost/focus state as URL params.
2) How should this integrate with existing filters? If a user filters to hide a service, ghosting should be disabled for that service (or ghost pill should show it as filtered).
3) What is default depth for focus across product tiers? Maybe advanced depth (All) behind a setting for enterprise.
4) How to surface correlation heuristics without confusing users—maybe a 'Related spans' toggle in the focus header.

Backlog tasks (first-cut):
- RED-UI-ghosting-01: implement ghost pill component + hover action (owner: Riley)
- RED-UI-focus-02: focus mode wireframe -> front-end prototype (owner: Avery)
- RED-ENG-perf-03: trace render perf test harness + 500-span dataset (owner: Samir)
- RED-UX-a11y-04: screen-reader testing pass & keyboard focus order doc (owner: Leah)
- RED-API-05: trace URL state encoding for shareable focus/ghost (owner: backend-team, dep on ticket RED-BE-982)

Prototype notes / rough implementation plan:
- Start with a front-end-only prototype toggling CSS classes for visual states; no data-model changes. Use a synthetic trace generator to create crowded lanes for demos.
- After initial UX signoff, implement a compacting strategy that defers to virtualization layer (row virtualization) to maintain render performance.
- Add telemetry events: ghost.toggle, focus.enter, focus.exit, focus.depth_changed so we can measure usage and reversal rates.

Sketch descriptions (for handoff to design):
- Sketch A: Hover toolbar expanded over span, ghost button highlighted, ghost pill top-right with counter.
- Sketch B: Focus header bar sitting above waveform timeline: includes 'exit', depth selector, spill toggle, and small legend showing ancestor/child colors.
- Sketch C: Compacting transition animation timeline (expand on hover, shrink on leave) with accessibility reduced-motion variant.

Notes to reviewers: please focus feedback on keyboard discoverability and the 'pointer-events' decision for ghosted spans. If we make ghosted spans non-clickable by default that reduces accidental clicks but may frustrate users who expect them to remain fully interactive.

Quick decision log (tentative):
- Decision: ghosting is additive and ephemeral (OK'd 2024-11-09 design sync).
- Tentative: default focus depth = 1; allow advanced users to set All via settings (awaiting PM sign-off).

Next steps:
- Riley to prototype ghost pill + hover affordance by EOD 2024-11-15.
- Front-end prototype review with design + SRE on 2024-11-18.
- Merge gating: ensure perf harness and accessibility test added before merging into main.

References / inspiration:
- Internal: span-selection keyboard flows (link in confluence).
- External: Observability UI patterns from commercial APMs and heatmap compaction patterns.

Raw sketch ascii (quick):
[Timeline axis]
|----|---------|-----------|---------|
Service A: [====      ] [=====   ] [=]
Service B: [ GHOSTED----] [---] [   ]
Service C (FOCUS) --> [=====FOCUS=====] [==]

(Key: ghosted lanes faded, focused lane bold)

End of notes.
